tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk not yet on its goal peg, clear any smaller disks that block it from moving, then move that largest disk to its goal peg before solving the remaining subproblem.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a disk is not in its goal position and larger disks are below it, requiring it to be moved after clearing smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move k disks from a source peg to a target peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk to the target, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to relocate a stack of disks while preserving order, using the third peg as temporary storage.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a stack of disks without first moving the smaller ones, leading to blocked moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last parseable list and ignores any preceding text.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final answer for the puzzle.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing the move list inside a paragraph or with missing brackets, causing the parser to fail.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Replay each move from the initial state and confirm that the resulting configuration exactly matches the goal before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating a move sequence, before finalizing the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that stops one step short of the goal, leading to a mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer should consist solely of the move list; any surrounding commentary, headings, or formatting can confuse the parser.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory sentences before the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk being moved and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a move would place a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg that still has disk 4 on top, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk will later need to be placed there, unless you first move the small disk away before the larger arrives.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting disk 1 onto the final goal peg before disk 4 is placed, causing later blockage.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk needs to be moved but is covered by smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disks 3 and 2 remain on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to output the moves after reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always conclude the response with a complete, syntactically correct move list.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may run out of tokens or lose track of the sequence, ending before reaching the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating moves, replay them to ensure the final configuration matches the goal; if not, continue adding moves.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the current peg state or assume a disk can be moved from anywhere.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit representation of each peg’s stack and check the top before each move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may place a small disk on the goal peg before the larger disks that belong below it have been placed.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only place a disk onto the goal peg when it is the next required disk in the final order.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook the size rule when selecting a destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
